comparison: Perfect agreement on sequence homology claims (C1, C2, C18, C19). Both evaluations find these straightforward bioinformatic analyses well-supported and foundational to the experimental design.

Strong agreement on STX2 electrophysiological phenotype (C7-C12 in OpenEval; C7-C17 in peer review). Both find the evoked release impairment data convincing. Peer review additionally includes spontaneous release claims (C13-C17) in this grouping.

Agreement on spontaneous release and fusogenicity data (C13-C17). OpenEval finds the data supported with C17 interpretive but reasonable. Peer review groups these with evoked release claims as part of core STX2 phenotype characterization.

Agreement on STX1A chimera electrophysiology (C20-C27 in OpenEval; C20-C26, C28-C33 in peer review). Both find the C-terminal half effects well-supported. Peer review groups additional claims (C28-C33) with this set.

Agreement on additional STX1A chimera parameters (C28-C33). OpenEval evaluates these separately from C20-C27, while peer review groups all STX1A chimera findings together as central to manuscript conclusions.

Agreement on neuronal survival rescue (C5, C6). OpenEval groups these with broader rescue data (C3, C4, C78), while peer review treats them as foundational controls establishing the experimental system validity.

Agreement on STX2 chimera findings (C34-C40 in OpenEval; C34-C38, C40-C45 in peer review). Both find partial rescue and domain regulatory conclusions well-supported. Peer review includes additional claims (C41-C45) in this grouping.

Agreement on STX2 chimera spontaneous release and RRP effects (C41-C45). OpenEval evaluates these separately, while peer review groups them with other STX2 chimera data as part of systematic reciprocal analysis.

Divergent evaluation of Munc18-1 correlation data for STX1A chimeras (C50-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to complex/contradictory patterns and unclear causal relationships. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting data quality while acknowledging interpretive complexity.

Divergent evaluation of Munc18-1 correlation data for STX2 chimeras (C56-C61). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to opposite trends versus STX1A chimeras and speculative mechanisms. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting data without questioning measurements or correlations.

Perfect agreement on point mutation findings (C62-C67). Both evaluations find the data well-supported and complementary to chimera conclusions, with mutations providing additional domain mapping granularity.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C68-C73). Both find conclusions about C-terminal half regulatory role well-supported by convergent evidence. OpenEval notes model (C71-C73) is speculative but reasonable; peer review emphasizes careful restriction of conclusions.

Agreement on overarching conclusion (C88). Both evaluations endorse the synthesis that SNARE domain has specific regulatory functions beyond membrane fusion, supported by comprehensive experimental evidence.
OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims (C46-C49, C74-C77, C79-C87) as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based claims.
